voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The southern Indian Ocean, nineteen seventy-nine. One American satellite saw a double flash. Vela satellites had seen forty-one before. Every one, a nuclear test.
But this witness was ten years old, past its design life. Its radio-pulse sensor had already failed.
Its two light sensors caught the flash. On the second pulse, they disagreed.
A panel for the White House suggested a meteoroid had struck the satellite, its debris catching the sun.
Later analysis judged a meteoroid much less likely, and other evidence pointed to a test. The United States has never confirmed what its satellite saw.
